summary: Geshe Jampa Tegchok (1930–2014) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology after studying at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1993) and as resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Gyume Tantric Monastery (attested 1987) and Sera Monastery (attested 1992).

Geshe Lhakdor (b. 1956) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery, he served at Tibet House, New Delhi (1986–1989) and became Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 2005.

Geshe Lhundub Sopa (1923–2014) studied at Gaden Chokor Monastery and Sera Jey Monastery under teachers including Lhundrub Thabkhe and Geshe Ngawang Rigsal. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he was an Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1967–1997).

Geshe Lobsang Choedar is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 2010, he held attested posts as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Lobsang Tenzin studied at Drepung Monastery. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric Monastery (attested 1987) and as Principal (1971) and Director (1988–2001) of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Geshe Lobsang Tharchin (1921–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Sera Monastery, earning his Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and also studied at Gyume Tantric Monastery.

Geshe Ngawang Nyima (1907–1990) specialized in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He held posts at Leiden University in 1960 and at Drepung Monastery as Geshe of sGo-mang sgrva-tshang (attested 1966 and 1995).

Geshe Ngawang Samten (b. 1956) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Ganden Shartse Monastery, later serving as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990–2019).

Geshe Palden Drakpa specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and worked as Librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi (attested 1987–1992 and 2004).

Geshe Rabten (1920–1986) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) and under Trijang Rinpoche, later teaching at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1969–1974).

Geshe Sonam Rinchen (1933–2013) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, later serving as resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from 1978.

Geshe Tashi Tsering (b. 1958) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1970–1987), Gyuto Monastery (~1987–1988), and under Geshe Thubten Rinchen, later becoming resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre in 1994.

Geshe Tenzin Dhargye (b. 1968) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1980–1995), Gyume Tantric Monastery (1995), and under Ling Rinpoche, later holding posts at Gyume Tantric Monastery, the University of Virginia, and Tibet Center Austria.
Geshe Tshondru Kongpel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed Geshe studies at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe (b. 1930) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held an attested post at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies in 1991 and served there as a scholar (attested 2001–2019).

Geshe Yeshe Tobden (1926–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) and under teachers including Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Lodrö Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche, later teaching Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin studied under Tenzin Gyatso, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki (1875–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. At Otani University, he served as a lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

Gherardo Gnoli (1937–2012) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies after studying at the University of Rome. He held professorial posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and the University of Rome (1993–2008).
